title: [spec-question] §28.10 / A5 vs K3.8: may a `using var` be the operand of `throw`? ("never movable out" vs the throw consume; r35 admits it, the model rejects it)
body:
**The question.** Axiom A5 (§28.3.2): *"`using var` is a scope pin: non-reassignable, never movable out"*; §28.3.7: *"A `using var` is owned but is additionally bound to its scope: it cannot be moved out of, only borrowed from (axiom A5)."* K3.8 (the consume table): the operand of `throw` is an owned-consuming position of an **owned binding**, post-state moved-from, marker-free, and §31.1 says the exception machinery takes ownership and disposes the exception after the arm. Nothing says whether the pin bars this consume. The text decides `Dispose()` (§28.6 lists a `using var` among admissible receivers) and the transfers (`move`, an `owned` argument, an owned-field store — all "moving out"), but not `throw`.

```bezel
using var c := new R(new Q());    // R derives from Exception
throw c;                          // A5: never movable out?  K3.8: a consume of an owned binding, disposed after the arm
```

**Readings.**
1. *A5 bars every obligation-moving consume* (the executable model's reading, bzcore L1: `consume_check` rejects any consume of a pin): `throw c` is a compile error; write `throw move c`-free spelling by declaring `c` with plain `var`. Consistent with A5's "declared intent" rationale (§5.23: scope-pinning is its entire meaning) and with the K4 bits: `throw` is obligation-moving (post-state moved-from), i.e. a move out of the scope.
2. *A5 bars the transfer rows only (K3.1–K3.4, K3.12) and reassignment*; the site-announced kills — `Dispose()`, the discard, `throw`, Pattern B `await` — are admitted on a pin because each sets the flag and the pin's scope end then finds an explicitly-disposed / moved binding. This is what r35 implements: `using var c := …; throw c;` compiles clean, and in a caught form `using var c; try throw c; catch var e: R => … end;` disposes the exception exactly once after the arm (measured: `D:2 D:1` once, the pin's scope end disposes nothing further).

**Recommendation.** State it in §28.10 either way; the model and the differential need one sentence. Reading 2 is memory-safe on r35 (measured, both modes) and keeps `throw` marker-free; reading 1 is the stricter declared-intent posture. If reading 2 is chosen, A5's "never movable out" should say "never transferred out (K3.1–K3.4, K3.12)".

**Differential numbers.** 51 of 6,000 sampled programs (try/while and all-features samples) are this shape, all accepted by r35 and rejected by the model as `A5-move-out-of-using-var`.

**Measured on r35** (`bezelc 0.0.0-f6863e62`, the 2026-10-27 release build; main may have moved since). Found by the model-vs-compiler differential (`scratch/bzdiff`, proposal 0047 §5.3 / soundness README §3.2).
